Correct. The misconception is that activity increases indefinitely with temperature. In reality, activity rises to an optimum then declines due to denaturation. Below the optimum the rate follows the Arrhenius equation, k = A·e^(−Ea/RT): from 25 °C to 35 °C the rate rises 189/124 = 1.52-fold, so ln(1.52) = (Ea/R)(1/298 − 1/308) gives Ea ≈ 32 kJ/mol. Above the optimum, thermal denaturation removes active enzyme and the rate falls (101 µmol/min at 55 °C).
